Package frc.DELib25.Subsystems.MotorSubsystems.MotorBase.MechanismSim

Class DCMotorMechanismSim

java.lang.Object
frc.DELib25.Subsystems.MotorSubsystems.MotorBase.MechanismSim.MechanismSim<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N2,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N2>
frc.DELib25.Subsystems.MotorSubsystems.MotorBase.MechanismSim.DCMotorMechanismSim
public class DCMotorMechanismSim extends MechanismSim<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N2,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N2>
Simulation helper for a mechanism driven by a DC motor with both position and velocity states.

This class models a second-order rotary system (states: [position, velocity]ᵀ) using a DC-motor plant (e.g., from LinearSystemId.createDCMotorSystem(edu.wpi.first.math.system.plant.DCMotor, double, double)). Use this when you care about angle tracking (turn-to-position, turret, etc.), not just speed.

How this differs from FlywheelSim:

  • DCMotorMechanismSim tracks position and velocity (2 states).
  • FlywheelSim tracks velocity only (1 state), which is ideal for shooters and wheels where absolute angle is irrelevant.

Units invalid input: '&' parameters:

  • Angle in radians (position), angular velocity in radians/second.
  • Moment of inertia J in kg·m² (about the output axis).
  • Gearing as output/input (e.g., 10:1 reduction → gearing = 10).

Notes:

  • Gravity torque is not inherently modeled; add a gravity feedforward if needed (for arms use LinearSystemId.createSingleJointedArmSystem(edu.wpi.first.math.system.plant.DCMotor, double, double)).
  • For speed-only mechanisms, prefer FlywheelSim.
